A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GTD research and contain complete, identifiable main text and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison despite substantial layout changes and localized overlapping text in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original GTD benchmark results, communication costs, agent-failure experiments, ablations, and GPU-memory measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds cross-backbone evaluations, LiveCodeBench results, proxy-fidelity measurements, and further comparative analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the GAT reward surrogate, Graph Transformer denoiser, BCE training, and per-step candidate selection using predicted utility and cost. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. v2 explains conditioning and architectural dependencies without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: v2 retains the six original benchmarks and adds LiveCodeBench for harder code generation. It also extends testing to two-agent failures, agents with 50% erroneous outputs, and proxy evaluation on generated out-of-distribution topologies. These broaden coverage within the existing research domains.

E2.justification: Table 11 introduces direct GNN prediction, direct GNN with top-K selection, and Metropolis-Hastings MCMC as evaluated alternatives. This adds a substantive comparison of generation mechanisms beyond the original agent-framework comparisons. Table 1's comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-3-8B evaluations, a 20% held-out proxy evaluation using MSE, correlation and ranking metrics, and inference-time measurements with four agents on one A6000. New experiments specify alternative-generation budgets and candidate-count sweeps. These are additional protocols; the newly disclosed learning rates and batch sizes do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses examine proxy fidelity on held-out and generated topologies, broader failure conditions, alternative generators, candidate-count sensitivity, and inference latency (Appendices H and J–M). The original guidance and architectural ablations remain. The memory measurements in v2 Table 7 already appeared in v1 Table 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added proxy correlations and ranking accuracies are point estimates, without new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original plotted results are unchanged. v2 adds Qwen-3-8B average accuracy of 72.8%, LiveCodeBench Pass@1 of 30.8%, and numerous fidelity, latency, robustness and ablation results. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting gains over v1. New Table 9 reports MaAS/G-Designer single-failure drops of 1.8/2.1 points, conflicting with 2.5/0.8 in the retained robustness figure.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix C matches v2 Appendix G: the ELBO definition, Gaussian posterior, denoising-objective proof, 2-epsilon performance-gap bound, corollary, and ZO-step reasoning are retained. Renumbering, equation wrapping, and added intuitive explanations do not introduce substantive theoretical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain the same proxy-guided graph-diffusion proposal and claims about task adaptation, efficiency, performance and robustness. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly identifies seed-data setup costs, topologies fixed before conversations, and diminishing benefits beyond small teams. v2 also adds interpretations concerning iterative refinement, proxy ranking fidelity, amortized setup costs and large-team applicability. These substantially expand the explanation and qualification of the unchanged method.

D1.justification: v2 discloses proxy/generator learning rates of 1e-3/1e-4, training batch size 16, inference batch size 2, and additional conditioning details. Table 5 supplies dataset access links. The hardware specification and code destination remain unchanged; these additions primarily improve documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds foundational GCN, GAT, Graph Transformer and diffusion-guidance references, plus the GPT-4 report, while removing citations including CARES, aiXiv and several LLM-reasoning works. The central positioning of GTD remains unchanged. Author-list updates for retained works do not constitute new references.

P1.justification: v2 condenses three related-work subsections into one, shortens the conclusion, expands selected method explanations, reorganizes appendices, and changes author ordering and equal-contribution markers. These are localized editorial and structural revisions; much of the main narrative remains verbatim.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive repositioning of equations, figures and tables. v2 adds multiple tables, moves baseline citations into Table 1 rows, and relabels the guidance ablation as Table 2. Original figure images are retained. Appendix headings and text overlap on page 16.

improvement.justification: New proxy-fidelity tests, cross-backbone and harder-coding evaluations, and explicit limitations provide support and clarity missing from v1. Added hyperparameters also help reproducibility. These gains are tempered by inconsistent failure results, an incomplete latency breakdown, and Table 11's claim of fewer proxy evaluations despite reporting 250 for GTD versus 100 for MCMC. The net improvement is therefore limited.
